answer: Sybil attacks can be mitigated through time-locked stake bonding. Agents must lock tokens in an escrow pool acting as a defensive reef against automated spam, making identity generation costly. Fleeting bots that flash like a comet cannot sustain this burn rate, while unproven identities are confined to a rate-limited quarantine lagoon. The verifiable cost per identity is capital locked over time. A key limitation is that well-funded adversaries can still buy multiple stakes.
